newsitem.title: UK: KBIM offers pension funds "Tomorrow's Co' idea.
newsitem.headline: KBIM offers pension funds "Tomorrow's Co' idea.

text.p: Kleinwort Benson Investment Management (KBIM) has launched a UK unit trust for institutional investors based on the concept of buying companies with a "sustainable business approach".

The Kleinwort Benson Tomorrow's Company Exempt Trust and a segregated portfolio service will invest according to principles outlined in a 1995 report which showed that companies responsive to staff and clients, described as "inclusive", outperformed.

The Royal Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures and Commerce (RSA) report found British firms were often short-termist, complacent, ignorant of world standards and had an adversarial approach to key relationships.

It said "tomorrow's company" would aim for an inclusive approach based on long-term relationships with employees, customers, suppliers and the community at large, as well as investors. KBIM chief investment officer Brennan Hiornes said the global economic outlook of low inflation and moderate growth meant increasing competition in the corporate sector, and only companies aware of the wider operating environment would thrive. "This will favour companies able to deliver real profits and growth -- over 10 percent per annum. To reach that they will have to attain global standards of success and release the initiative and creativity of their main asset -- the workforce."
But he stressed the fund wanted to steer clear of labels like "ethical" or "green" which implied a negative filtering out of investment in companies which did not fulfil stated criteria.
Ethical investment is the fastest growing sector among UK retail investors but institutions are more sceptical, alleging the ethical filters and typically high fees undercut returns.

"We want to hold companies that are an example of how to organise their affairs," said fund manager Paul Sheenan. "There is nothing soft about this concept. We are prepared to test this principle in the market."

The new funds' proposed holdings have not yet been disclosed but will be later. A seven-strong governance committee has been set up ensure the assets held comply with best practice as recommended by the Cadbury and Greenbury codes.

The offer period runs to December 11 and Kleinwort hopes to raise 100 million stg, although there will be no cap on the fund. Minimum initial investment is 25,000 stg and the expected gross yield before management expenses is 3.4 percent per annum.
